title: Best Beaches in Maharashtra: Konkan Coast from Alibaug to Tarkarli

metaDescription: The best beaches on Maharashtra's Konkan coast: Alibaug, Kashid, Shrivardhan, Guhagar, Ganpatipule, Tarkarli and Malvan, with sea forts and turtles.
description: A guide to the best beaches on Maharashtra's Konkan coast, from Alibaug, Nagaon and Kashid near Mumbai to Murud-Janjira, Diveagar, Shrivardhan and Harihareshwar, the Blue Flag beaches of Guhagar and Ladghar, Velas and its turtles, Ganpatipule, and Tarkarli, Devbagh and Malvan in Sindhudurg, with seasons, access and safety.
dek: The Konkan coast mixes beaches with sea forts, temples and seafood towns. Here are the best beaches in Maharashtra, from weekend escapes near Mumbai to Sindhudurg's clear water.

intro: Maharashtra's coast, the northern Konkan, runs for about 720 km from Palghar near Gujarat to the Goa border. It is a coast of small beaches between rocky headlands and river mouths, many of them guarded by sea forts built or rebuilt under the Marathas. Beaches closer to Mumbai, such as Alibaug and Kashid, are busy weekend escapes; further south, in Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg districts, they get quieter and the water clearer.
In 2025, five Maharashtra beaches, Shrivardhan, Nagaon, Parnaka, Guhagar and Ladghar, received Blue Flag certification. This guide goes from north to south.
quickAnswer: The best beaches in Maharashtra are Alibaug, Nagaon and Kashid near Mumbai, Diveagar, Shrivardhan and Harihareshwar in Raigad, Guhagar, Ganpatipule and the turtle beach at Velas in Ratnagiri, and Tarkarli, Devbagh and Malvan in Sindhudurg, the best for snorkelling and try dives. Visit from October to March. Swimming is unsafe in the monsoon, when many Konkan beaches are closed to bathing.
takeaways: Alibaug, Nagaon and Kashid are the easiest beach weekends from Mumbai, partly by ferry.
Shrivardhan, Nagaon, Parnaka, Guhagar and Ladghar received Blue Flag certification in 2025.
Tarkarli and Malvan in Sindhudurg have the clearest water, with snorkelling and scuba try dives.
Velas in Ratnagiri is known for olive ridley turtle hatchlings, mostly from about February to April.
Konkan beaches are rough and closed to swimming in the monsoon (June to September).

rows: Evening walks and street food (not swimming)

items.name: Mumbai's city beaches
body: Juhu and Girgaon Chowpatty are for evening walks, sunsets and street food, not swimming; the water is not clean and currents are strong.

items.name: Alibaug, Nagaon and Kihim
body: Across the harbour from Mumbai, reached by ferry from the Gateway of India area to Mandwa plus a short drive, or by road. Kolaba Fort sits offshore from Alibaug beach and can be reached on foot at low tide. Nagaon has water sports and Blue Flag certification.

facts.From Mumbai: About 2 to 3 hours by ferry and road

items.name: Kashid
body: About 30 km south of Alibaug, Kashid has pale sand, casuarina trees and water sports, and gets crowded on weekends.

items.name: Murud and Janjira
body: From Rajpuri jetty near Murud, sailboats cross to Murud-Janjira, an island fort that was never captured. Murud itself has a quiet beach.

items.name: Diveagar, Shrivardhan and Harihareshwar
body: Three quieter beaches further south in Raigad: Diveagar with casuarina groves, Shrivardhan with Blue Flag certification, and Harihareshwar, a temple town on a rocky headland.

items.name: Velas
body: A small village beach where a local conservation effort protects olive ridley turtle nests. Hatchlings are released on the beach mostly from about February to April, and the village holds a turtle festival with homestays. Sightings depend entirely on nature; there are no guaranteed dates.

facts.Good to know: Early mornings and evenings; follow volunteers' rules

items.name: Dapoli coast
body: Ladghar (Blue Flag), Karde and Murud near Dapoli are quiet beaches, with dolphin-spotting boat trips from Karde and Ladghar in the calm season.

items.name: Guhagar
body: A long, clean beach backed by a small temple town, with Blue Flag certification.

items.name: Ganpatipule
body: A temple town whose Swayambhu Ganapati temple stands right by the beach. The coast road north to Aare-Ware has some of the Konkan's best views.

items.name: Tarkarli and Devbagh
body: Tarkarli has a long beach with clear water in season and backwaters along the Karli river behind it. Devbagh sits on the spit where river and sea meet. Snorkelling trips, scuba try dives and houseboat rides are offered, and the Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation runs a scuba institute here.

items.name: Malvan
body: A fishing town known for Malvani seafood, and the jetty for boats to Sindhudurg Fort, built by Shivaji in the 17th century on an island just offshore.

items.name: Vengurla and Shiroda
body: Quiet beaches close to the Goa border, good for combining with north Goa.

sections.heading: Getting there
list: Ferries from the Gateway of India area to Mandwa (with onward transport to Alibaug) are the quickest route to Alibaug; they do not run in the monsoon.
The Konkan Railway serves Ratnagiri, Kudal and Sindhudurg for the southern beaches.
The Mumbai to Goa highway (NH66) runs inland; coastal roads and river crossings reach the beaches.
Sindhudurg airport near Chipi and Goa's airports serve Tarkarli and Malvan.

safety: Swim only at beaches with lifeguards, inside the flagged zone, and never when a red flag is up or during the monsoon.
Many Konkan beaches have strong currents and steep shelves; swim only where locals and lifeguards say it is safe.
Walking to Kolaba Fort at low tide is only safe with enough time before the tide returns; check tide times.
Do not swim in the monsoon; drownings happen every year.
At Velas, follow volunteers' rules: no torches, flash or crowding near hatchlings.
packing: A light jacket for ferry rides

faqs.q: Which is the best beach in Maharashtra?
faqs.a: Tarkarli in Sindhudurg for clear water and snorkelling; Kashid and Alibaug for weekends from Mumbai; Guhagar and Ganpatipule for quieter stays.

faqs.q: Which Maharashtra beaches have Blue Flag certification?
faqs.a: Shrivardhan, Nagaon, Parnaka, Guhagar and Ladghar, certified in 2025.

faqs.q: When can I see turtles at Velas?
faqs.a: Hatchlings are released mostly from about February to April; timings depend on nature.

faqs.q: Can I swim at Juhu or Chowpatty?
faqs.a: It is not advisable; the water is polluted and currents are strong.

faqs.q: How do I reach Alibaug from Mumbai?
faqs.a: By ferry from the Gateway of India area to Mandwa and then road, or by road via the Mumbai to Goa highway.
